summary: This episode describes the religious and social climate of Mecca before prophethood, full of superstition, then introduces the hanifs who rejected idols, especially Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, the cousin of Umar al-Khattab. Alone, he was condemned by his people for rejecting idols, rebuked sacrifice for idols, rescued and raised girls who were about to be buried alive, and travelled in search of the true religion of Ibrahim. He was robbed and killed on the way home, before meeting the Prophet ﷺ, but his prayer for his son Said was answered, and his daughter Atikah married five martyrs. The Prophet ﷺ said he would be resurrected as a community of one. The ustaz closes with reflections on the ten quiet years in the Prophet's ﷺ life before revelation and why we need to think deeply, because the Quraysh's condition is in fact our condition.
keyPoints: Quraysh society was full of superstition such as azlam, bird omens and unlucky numbers, and the ustaz shows that similar forms still exist today.
The hanifs were people who rejected idols and claimed to follow the religion of Ibrahim, but did not know what that religion really was.
Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufayl stood alone against idol worship, forbade adultery and rescued girls about to be buried alive, though he had no revelation.
He once refused to eat meat slaughtered for idols in front of the young Prophet ﷺ.
He was robbed and killed on the way home after being told the final prophet would emerge from his homeland, and prayed that his son Said not be kept from meeting the Prophet.
The Prophet ﷺ said Zaid would be resurrected as a community of one, and saw him in Paradise.
The ten quiet years before revelation invite us to reflect on whether our hearts are locked even though we hear lectures every day.

chapters.title: Quraysh superstition and today's
chapters.summary: Azlam, birds and Quraysh omens, with similar examples today such as lift numbers, black cats and unlucky dates.

chapters.title: The hanifs
chapters.summary: Four hanifs rejected idols and claimed to follow the religion of Ibrahim but did not know how.

chapters.title: Waraqah, Uthman and Ubaydullah
chapters.summary: Three hanifs searched for the truth in Sham, Rome and Abyssinia with different endings.

chapters.title: Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufayl
chapters.summary: An introduction to Zaid, Umar's cousin, and his story narrated by Zaid ibn Harithah.

chapters.title: Meeting the young Prophet ﷺ
chapters.summary: The Prophet asked why his people condemned Zaid, and Zaid replied that he left his people's religion and followed the religion of Ibrahim.

chapters.title: Refusing meat slaughtered for idols
chapters.summary: Zaid told the Prophet that he ate only what was slaughtered in Allah's name.

chapters.title: Calling to the truth, and prayer at the Kaaba
chapters.summary: Zaid rebuked sacrifice for idols and prostrated toward the Kaaba without being taught how.

chapters.title: Al-Khattab's hostility to Zaid
chapters.summary: Umar's father hired people to hurt Zaid and guarded the border so he could not enter Mecca.

chapters.title: Travelling in search of religion
chapters.summary: Zaid learned from monks in Sham, found tawhid mixed with shirk, and returned secretly at night.

chapters.title: Forbidding adultery, and poverty
chapters.summary: Zaid forbade adultery because it inherits poverty, linked by the ustaz to a study of cases of underage marriage.

chapters.title: Saving the girls
chapters.summary: Zaid forbade killing girls and raised them, then asked whether the father wanted to take her back.

chapters.title: The last journey to Mosul
chapters.summary: At 85 Zaid reached Mosul and was told the final prophet would emerge from his homeland, then he was robbed and killed.

chapters.title: The prayer for Zaid's son and descendants
chapters.summary: His prayer was answered: Said was promised Paradise, and Atikah married five martyrs.

chapters.title: Zaid's greeting to the Prophet ﷺ
chapters.summary: Amir ibn Rabiah conveyed Zaid's greeting, and the Prophet ﷺ returned it.

chapters.title: A community of one
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said Zaid would be resurrected as a community and seen in Paradise in a long garment with two trees shading him.

chapters.title: Ten quiet years and a locked heart
chapters.summary: The ustaz asks why the Prophet ﷺ reflected deeply before revelation, and whether our hearts are locked even though we hear lectures.

books.context: The ustaz mentions the long Bukhari hadith about Zaid going to learn from monks in Sham.
books.note: Author not named in the lecture: Imam Bukhari

people.context: Studied the Torah and Gospel in Sham and looked for the final prophet.
A Meccan who went to Rome, held a high position and died in the Christian religion.
Migrated to Abyssinia; a weak report says he returned to Christianity.
Stood alone against idol worship and rescued girls; died robbed before meeting the Prophet ﷺ.
Narrated Zaid ibn Amr's meeting with the young Prophet ﷺ while they rode together.
Narrated Zaid's deeds in Mecca, including rescuing girls.
Hated Zaid intensely, hired people to hurt him and guarded the border.
One of the ten Companions promised Paradise; Umar accepted Islam through his house.
Married Zaid ibn al-Khattab, Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr, Umar, Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Hasan ibn Ali.
Zaid's cousin; accepted Islam through his sister Fatimah and Said ibn Zaid.
Conveyed Zaid's greeting to the Prophet ﷺ.

lessons.title: Dare to differ on principle
lessons.body: Zaid stood alone against the practices of a whole city though he was cursed and stoned, for the truth he believed in.

lessons.title: A caring conscience
lessons.body: Zaid cared for the girls though there was no material benefit, indeed a burden, something that makes no sense to a materially obsessed society.

lessons.title: Think with reason, not superstition
lessons.body: Even educated people can fall into irrational beliefs such as unlucky numbers, black cats and dates.

lessons.title: Social ills inherit poverty
lessons.body: The ustaz links the prohibition of adultery to inherited poverty, based on a study of court files on underage marriage.

lessons.title: A father's prayer protects his descendants
lessons.body: Zaid's prayer that his son not be kept from meeting the Prophet was answered, and his descendants were looked after by the best Companions.

lessons.title: Hold your conviction even when alone
lessons.body: Though he had no revelation and did not live to meet the Prophet, Zaid is resurrected as a community for defending his belief.

lessons.title: What we do with the knowledge we have
lessons.body: We already have the Quran, hadith and many classes; the question is what we do with that knowledge, like Zaid who cared about the hardship around him.

lessons.title: Think deeply and be aware of our actions
lessons.body: Life today wipes out thinking so that many of our actions simply follow the crowd; the Prophet's ﷺ process of deep thinking is worth reflecting on.

lessons.title: Check whether our hearts are locked
lessons.body: Even if we hear lectures and read religious books, the heart can be locked without our knowing, and we do not make the effort to open it.

lessons.title: The Quraysh's condition is our condition
lessons.body: Many read the sirah without realising that what is told about the Quraysh is a picture of our own state.

glossary.meaning: Arrows the Quraysh used to make decisions, such as whether to travel.
The mind's ability to think logically, which the ustaz says often fails when it comes to superstitious beliefs.
One who rejected idols and claimed to follow the religion of Ibrahim in the era before prophethood.
A community of one; Zaid is resurrected alone but stands as a community.
Deep reflection on the verses of the Quran, stressed by the ustaz as an injection to make us think more deeply.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions it as a narration of Zaid ibn Harithah showing that Zaid ibn Amr sparked thought in the Prophet ﷺ.
dalil.translation: When the young Prophet ﷺ was served meat slaughtered for idols, Zaid ibn Amr said, my nephew, do not eat from this meat; I eat only what is slaughtered in Allah's name.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Asma bint Abi Bakr related it in a sirah narration.
dalil.translation: Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufayl gave life to girls about to be buried alive by saying do not kill her, I will look after her welfare.

dalil.context: The ustaz links Zaid's act to the verse that the buried girl will be asked for what sin she was killed. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: when the baby girl buried alive is asked

dalil.context: Mentioned in the story of Zaid, who did not live to meet the Prophet ﷺ.
dalil.translation: Amir ibn Rabiah conveyed to the Prophet ﷺ that Zaid had said if he met the Prophet he would believe, and the Prophet ﷺ returned his greeting.

dalil.context: Said ibn Zaid and Umar asked the Prophet ﷺ about Zaid's fate.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufayl will be resurrected on the Day of Judgement alone but as a community, and told them to ask forgiveness for him.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions three narrations describing the honour given to Zaid in Paradise.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said he saw Zaid in a long garment in Paradise, two great trees shading him, and that he dwelt on two levels of Paradise.

sirah.summary: This episode describes the religious and social climate of Mecca before the Prophet ﷺ was sent through the story of the hanifs, especially Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, and the quiet ten years in the Prophet's ﷺ life.
